saints.name: Sts. Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen
saints.title: Bishops and Doctors of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: Two friends of Cappadocia who defended the Nicene faith against Arianism and shaped the theology of the Holy Trinity…
biography: Basil was born about 330 at Caesarea in Cappadocia; Gregory, about 329 at Arianzus, was the son of the bishop of Nazianzus. The two became fast friends as students at Athens and later shared the monastic retreat Basil founded at Annesi in Pontus.

Consecrated bishop of Caesarea in 370, Basil wrote his treatise On the Holy Spirit, stood unmoved before the Arian emperor Valens, and organized the monastic life of the East. He built the Basiliad, a poorhouse, hospice, and hospital that Gregory likened to a new wonder of the world; hence his patronage of monks and of hospital administrators. He died on 1 January 379.

Gregory, ordained priest by his father in 361 and consecrated bishop of Sasima against his will in 372, was called to Constantinople in 379. There his five Theological Orations on the Trinity won the Arian capital back to Nicaea and earned him the lasting title of the Theologian.

Enthroned by the emperor Theodosius, he presided at the Council of Constantinople in 381, then resigned for the sake of peace and died in retirement on 25 January 390. Both are Doctors of the Church, among the four great Doctors of the East.
saints.knownFor: Defending the Nicene faith and articulating the doctrine of the Trinity.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; Doctors of the Church
